answer: Stop sybils with a thread, a horizon lock, and a karst audit. Each identity earns standing through one thread: endorsements from unrelated peers, each link sealed to its bond and the prior link, so a copy cannot reuse a link without forging the chain. The horizon lock releases standing in stages, each demanding an endorsement from outside the funding cluster, so shells queue. A karst audit samples one thread per epoch and traces it to its funder root; when N copies converge on one root, all N are slashed together, each losing a multiple of the linked count, so N clones cost N squared bonds.
